terms.definition: Recognizing revenue when earned and expenses when incurred, regardless of cash timing.
Spreading the cost of a definite-lived intangible asset (e.g., acquired customer relationships, capitalized software) over its useful life; non-cash.
Basic = common shares outstanding; diluted adds the net effect of in-the-money options, warrants, and convertibles via the treasury stock or if-converted method.
A stock's systematic risk relative to the market (market beta = 1.0); an input to CAPM for estimating cost of equity.
A GP's request that LPs fund a portion of their committed capital to finance investments or fees.
Capital Asset Pricing Model: cost of equity = risk-free rate + beta × equity risk premium.
The GP's share of fund profits, typically 20%, earned after LPs have received their preferred return.
A waterfall tier where the GP takes a large share (often 100%) of distributions until it reaches its target carry percentage on all profit above return of capital.
A provision requiring the GP to return previously distributed carry if, at fund wind-down, it was overpaid relative to final fund performance.
A direct investment into a specific portfolio company made alongside a lead GP, outside the main fund, typically with no management fee or carry.
The total capital an LP pledges to a fund; it is called over time rather than wired up front.
Valuation methodology using public peers' trading multiples to estimate the value of a target company.
A new fund a GP forms to hold assets rolled out of an aging fund, giving existing LPs the option to cash out or roll in; a GP-led secondary.
The extra price a buyer pays to acquire control of a company versus its public trading price; the reason precedent transaction multiples typically exceed trading comp multiples.
The interest rate on a company's borrowings; used after-tax in WACC because interest expense is tax-deductible.
The required return of equity holders; estimated via CAPM as risk-free rate + beta × equity risk premium.
Timing differences between book and tax accounting: a DTL arises when book tax expense exceeds cash taxes now; a DTA arises when cash taxes exceed book expense (e.g., NOL carryforwards).
Spreading the cost of tangible PP&E over its useful life; non-cash, reduces taxable income, added back in CFO.
A PME method that solves for the exact annualized rate of outperformance or underperformance versus a public index.
Cash (or occasionally stock) returned by a PE fund to its LPs as investments are exited or recapitalized.
Raising new debt at a portfolio company to fund a distribution to the PE sponsor, pulling forward equity returns without an exit.
Distributions to Paid-In capital; the realized, cash-in-hand multiple (cumulative distributions ÷ paid-in capital).
Discounted cash flow valuation: project unlevered free cash flows, discount at WACC to get enterprise value, then bridge to equity value.
Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization; a widely used proxy for operating cash generation and the most common LBO and M&A valuation metric.
The value of the entire operating business independent of capital structure; EV = Equity Value + Debt + Preferred + Minority Interest − Cash.
Value attributable to common shareholders; diluted shares × share price.
The expected return of the equity market over the risk-free rate; an input to CAPM, commonly estimated at 4–6%.
The EV/EBITDA assumed at sale of the portfolio company; used for terminal value in a DCF and for LBO exit equity calculation.
Cash to all capital providers before interest: NOPAT + D&A − capex − ΔNWC; discounted at WACC to yield enterprise value.
Cash to equity holders after interest and mandatory debt repayment; discounted at cost of equity to yield equity value directly.
The fund manager who sources, executes, and exits investments and bears unlimited liability.
Terminal value as a growing perpetuity: TV = FCF_n × (1 + g) ÷ (WACC − g); g must be below WACC and is typically capped near GDP/inflation.
Gross IRR is before fund-level fees and carry; net IRR is after all fees, expenses, and carry — the LP's actual return; the spread is fee drag.
The minimum annualized return LPs must receive (commonly ~8%) before the GP earns carried interest.
Diluted share calculation for convertible securities: if in the money, add the shares they convert into and remove the related after-tax interest expense.
The annualized discount rate that sets the net present value of an investment's cash flows to zero; time-sensitive and can be gamed by timing of capital calls.
The early-life dip in PE fund returns caused by management fees and undeployed capital before exits occur; the curve recovers as investments mature and are realized.
Acquisition of a company funded largely with debt that the target's own cash flows repay over a 3–7 year hold; return drivers are EBITDA growth, multiple expansion, and deleveraging.
A fund investor who commits capital, has limited liability, and receives distributions; cannot participate in management.
The original PME method (1996) that produces an IRR from a synthetic public-market investment; can break (negative NAV) when fund performance is very strong.
PME method (2005) returning a ratio (>1.0 = fund beat the index); avoids negative-NAV breakdown and is the most widely accepted PME measure.
Annual fee paid to the GP, commonly ~2% on committed capital during the investment period and on invested/net cost thereafter.
Discounting explicit cash flows at periods 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, ... to reflect that cash arrives throughout the year rather than at year-end; modestly raises DCF value.
The portion of a consolidated subsidiary not owned by the parent company; added in the EV bridge to match the fully consolidated EBITDA denominator.
Multiple on Invested Capital: total equity proceeds ÷ equity invested; a cash-on-cash multiple that ignores the time value of money.
Net asset value; the GP's fair-value mark of remaining unrealized fund holdings under ASC 820/IFRS 13.
Fund-level borrowing secured against the whole portfolio; used to fund follow-on investments or, controversially, to fund LP distributions without underlying exits.
Total debt minus cash and cash equivalents; the net financial obligation used in the EV-to-equity bridge.
Operating current assets (AR, inventory, prepaids) minus operating current liabilities (AP, accrued expenses); excludes cash and short-term debt.
Net operating profit after tax: EBIT × (1 − tax rate); the starting point for unlevered free cash flow.
Cumulative capital actually called and funded by LPs to date; always less than or equal to total commitment.
Public Market Equivalent; a family of methods that benchmark a PE fund against a public index by replicating the fund's cash-flow timing in the index.
Valuation methodology using multiples paid in past M&A deals for comparable targets; typically yields higher values than trading comps due to control premiums.
A financing claim senior to common equity in dividends and liquidation; added in the EV bridge because it is part of the capital funding the enterprise.
Residual Value to Paid-In: the unrealized, GP-marked portion of fund value (residual NAV ÷ paid-in capital).
The buying and selling of existing LP fund interests (LP-led) or GP-initiated restructurings (GP-led); more mature positions with the J-curve largely behind them.
The LBO funding table showing where money comes from (debt, sponsor equity, rollover) and where it goes (purchase price, fees, balance sheet cash); total sources must equal total uses.
Non-cash equity compensation to employees; deducted on the income statement but added back in CFO on the cash flow statement.
The value of all cash flows beyond the explicit DCF forecast period; estimated via Gordon growth model or exit multiple; typically drives 60–80% of total DCF value.

Estimating net dilutive shares from in-the-money options: assumes exercise proceeds are used to repurchase shares at the current market price; net new shares = options exercised minus shares repurchased.
Total Value to Paid-In: DPI + RVPI; the combined realized and unrealized multiple and the total fund scorecard.
The year a fund begins investing; the standard unit of benchmarking because macroeconomic conditions at entry dominate fund outcomes.
Weighted Average Cost of Capital: the blended required return across all capital (equity and debt), used to discount unlevered free cash flows to enterprise value.
The profit-split order in a PE fund: American (deal-by-deal) lets the GP take carry per profitable exit; European (whole-fund) requires all LP capital and preferred be returned before any GP carry.
The period-over-period change in net working capital; an increase in NWC uses cash and is subtracted in the free cash flow build.
